caption: Session Context
description: A native record reporting the session's settings, context injected into the model's input (system reminders, attachments, developer messages), or accounting at session, response or child-run scope (usage/cost). These are supporting facts; they are not submissions, responses or tool calls.
name: session_context

1.caption: Settings reported
1.description: A record reporting launch or session settings was observed.

2.caption: Context injected
2.description: A record reporting context injected into the model input was observed.

3.caption: Accounting reported
3.description: A record reporting session-, response- or child-run-scope usage or cost accounting was observed.

4.caption: Outcome reported
4.description: The CLI reports how its run or session ended (an exit code, a lifecycle state, a cancellation flag) in its own record. It is the CLI's report, kept apart from Journal's observation of the process.

5.caption: State reported
5.description: The source reports task or plan state. No model invocation, prompt submission or tool lifecycle stage is inferred.

cli_agent.description: The CLI agent is stored once per run in run.json shared.cli_agent; it is present on an event only in a self-contained export.

response_uid.description: The response an accounting record cites, when it names one.

tool_call_uid.description: The tool call whose spawned child run an accounting record reports (usage at scope 7 Child run), as the source names it; absent otherwise. It identifies the unit, never a second tool call.

content_blocks.description: The injected content as rendered to the model, when the source reports it as blocks.

basis.description: The mapping rule that classified this record.

exit_code.description: The exit code the CLI reports in its own outcome record (Outcome reported); Journal's observation of the process is declared separately.

reported_state.description: The outcome or lifecycle state exactly as the source reports it.

assembly.description: Present in a finally assembled file: this event's assembly role and evidence.

data.description: The native record exactly as reported.

duration.description: The source-reported elapsed execution time in integral milliseconds. No start/end timestamps or aggregation window are inferred. Exact non-integral durations use execution_metrics in their native unit.
